claim: Baiersbronn's Michelin Guide listing of its three-star restaurants — Schwarzwaldstube and Restaurant Bareiss.
quote: Baiersbronn 3 Stars MICHELIN Restaurants — the MICHELIN Guide Germany.

claim: Baiersbronn's 2025 Michelin Guide tally: two 3-star, no 2-star, two 1-star — eight stars across four restaurants; Lumpp received the Mentor Chef award.
quote: Three-Star: Bareiss, Schwarzwaldstube. One-Star: 1789, Schlossberg. Two-Star: None. Total: 8 stars across four establishments. Lumpp received the 'Mentor Chef' award.

claim: Schwarzwaldstube has held three Michelin stars continuously since 1993 — the longest streak for any German restaurant; Torsten Michel has been head chef since 2017.
quote: Has maintained its three-star Michelin rating continuously since 1993—the longest streak for any German restaurant. Torsten Michel has served as head chef since 2017.

claim: Torsten Michel (born Dresden 1977) joined Schwarzwaldstube in 2004, became sole head chef in 2017, and trained at The Fat Duck, Noma, and L'Arnsbourg.
quote: Michel joined the Schwarzwaldstube in January 2004 ... In 2017 he took over sole leadership ... internships at The Fat Duck, Noma, and L'Arnsbourg.

claim: Schwarzwaldstube has 36 seats with floor-to-ceiling windows over the Tonbach Valley; signature dishes include poached Gillardeau oysters with caviar and Alsatian pigeon breast.
quote: Modern, elegant dining room (36 seats max). Floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking Tonbach Valley and Black Forest. Signature: Poached Gillardeau oysters with Imperial caviar; Alsatian pigeon breast with liquorice.

claim: Schwarzwaldstube charges €325 for its 7-course tasting menu; open Wed–Fri evenings and Sat–Sun lunch + dinner; Gault Millau 20.2/20.
quote: €325 for 7-course tasting menu (includes amuse-bouche and petit fours). Wednesday-Friday: 7:00 PM – 10:00 PM. Saturday-Sunday: 12:00 PM – 2:00 PM and 7:00 PM – 10:00 PM. Gault Millau Score: 20.2/20.

claim: Schwarzwaldstube is the three-star flagship of the Traube Tonbach hotel at Tonbachstraße 237, Baiersbronn.

Restaurant Bareiss is open Thursday–Sunday, lunch from 12:00 and dinner from 19:00; closed Mon–Wed; 2026 closures Feb 9–Mar 6 and Jul 27–Aug 28; phone +49 7442 47-0; head chef Claus-Peter Lumpp with pâtissier Stefan Leitner.
quote: Thursday–Sunday: Lunch from 12:00 p.m., Dinner from 7:00 p.m. Closed Monday–Wednesday. 2026 closures: Feb 9–Mar 6, Jul 27–Aug 28. Phone: +49 7442 47-0.

claim: Restaurant Bareiss offers a 7-course menu around €258, a 6-course around €210, and a 3-course lunch at €130; classical French technique, dessert trolley is a standout.
quote: Evening options include a 7-course menu (€258) and shorter 6-course option (€210). 3-course lunch menu cost €130. Extensive dessert trolley with macaroons, pralines, tarts, and cakes.

claim: Restaurant Bareiss reopened mid-March 2024 after a three-week renovation; new look uses matte brass with velvet green tones, presented as a 60th-birthday gift to Lumpp.
quote: Mid-March 2024 reopening after three-week renovation. 'Goldschimmerndes, mattiertes Messing und ein samtiges Grün' (matte brass with velvet green). Presented as 60th-birthday gift to Lumpp.

claim: Baiersbronn (population ~14,000) sits in Germany's 2,300-square-mile Black Forest; competition between the Traube Tonbach (1789) and Hotel Bareiss (1951) drove its rise as a culinary destination.
quote: Baiersbronn is a community of 14,000 people nestled in Germany's Black Forest, a 2,300-square-mile region. A hospitality arms race between Traube Tonbach (opened 1789) and competitor Hotel Bareiss (opened 1951) drove culinary excellence upward.

claim: Forum consensus: jacket and tie expected at Baiersbronn's 3-star rooms; jeans, t-shirts and sneakers are inappropriate.
quote: Collared shirt, jacket and tie, proper pants (no jeans) and ditto shoes - that's the minimum for formal occasions. Jeans, t-shirts, caps, and sneakers should be avoided.

claim: Hotel Bareiss formally requests guests dress appropriately for dinner out of respect for other guests.
quote: Dress appropriately for dinner ... out of respect and consideration for other guests.

claim: Baiersbronn tourism office's gourmet roster: two three-star restaurants (Bareiss, Schwarzwaldstube) and two one-star restaurants (1789, Schlossberg).
quote: Three-Star: Restaurant Bareiss, Schwarzwaldstube. One-Star: 1789, Gourmetrestaurant Schlossberg. No two-star Michelin restaurants are mentioned.

claim: Hotel Bareiss accepts table enquiries via an online form or by phone at +49 7442 47-0; the form requires date, party size, contact details, and notes whether you've stayed before.
quote: Submit a table enquiry through their online form, or contact the reservation team directly at +49 7442 47-0.

claim: German national press confirms Baiersbronn's eight-star tally in the 2025 Michelin Guide Germany across the same four restaurants.
quote: Three-Star Restaurants: Schwarzwaldstube (Torsten Michel), Bareiss (Claus-Peter Lumpp). One-Star Restaurants: 1789 (Florian Stolte), Schlossberg (Nico Sackmann).

claim: Schlossberg at Hotel Sackmann (Jörg and Nico Sackmann) currently holds one Michelin star, down from two stars between 2014 and 2018.
quote: Schlossberg currently awarded a Michelin star. Between 2014 and 2018, the restaurant was awarded two Michelin stars.

claim: Recent (March 2025) Schwarzwaldstube review: pigeon with liquorice, Norwegian lobster with Asian flavours, and a bee-sting cake dessert; Michel visits tables after the savoury courses.
quote: Alsatian pigeon with licorice and lemon thyme; Pan-fried Norwegian lobster with Asian-inspired flavors; Bee sting cake. The head chef personally visits tables following the savory courses.

claim: Traube Tonbach's own travel notes: about 1 h 30 min by car from Stuttgart Airport and about 1 h 10 min from Strasbourg.
quote: Located in the heart of the Black Forest, between Strasbourg, Stuttgart and Freiburg; ~1h29m drive from Stuttgart Airport; ~1h07m from Strasbourg.
